tools.name: validate_email
tools.description: Free. Check the syntax of an email address offline and get the normalized address and domain, before paying for check_email_address. No DNS lookup, no network request, no payment.

tools.name: pricing
tools.description: Free. Return the price of check_email_address (and of the HTTP-only email test report), the payment network (Base) and the receiving address. No input, no network request, no payment.

tools.name: check_email_address
tools.description: Check one email address before you send to it: syntax, whether the domain accepts mail (MX, null MX or implicit A record), a disposable-domain flag (public CC0 list of about 9,900 domains), a role-account flag (info@, support@, noreply@...) and a free-provider flag. tools.name: email_fix_plan
tools.description: Get an email security fix plan for one domain: the exact SPF, DKIM and DMARC DNS records to publish (create / replace / keep, record name, value and why), in order, plus click-path steps for the domain's DNS host (Cloudflare, GoDaddy, Route 53, Namecheap, Squarespace/Google, Vercel and others). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_email, check_email_address, email_fix_plan · Private data: check_email_address, email_fix_plan · Public sink: validate_email, pricing, check_email_address, email_fix_plan.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_email, check_email_address, email_fix_plan · Private data: check_email_address, email_fix_plan · Public sink: validate_email, pricing, check_email_address, email_fix_plan

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
